IO

Invoice OCR Viewer

how it works - layout on the CPU, recognition on the GPU, everything on this Mac

01How a request flows

The backend handles everything between upload and JSON. Inference runs one page at a time behind a lock - no queue service.

1 - Upload

read_upload_capped

Streamed in 1 MB chunks and cut off at 10 MB, so a file that is too big fails fast - before it is ever held in memory.

2 - Normalize

load_normalized

Read by content, never by file extension. EXIF-rotated, re-encoded as PNG - and those exact bytes are what inference sees.

3 - Infer

RealPipeline

Check the MLX server is up, then run the pipeline: layout on the CPU, recognition sent block by block to the GPU. The model loads once and is reused; temp files are always cleaned up.

4 - Shape

normalize_blocks

Raw pipeline output becomes plain JSON: blocks in reading order, table HTML sanitized against an allowlist, temp-file paths stripped.

02Why the boxes always line up

The boxes line up because there is nothing to convert:

  • The backend normalizes the image first and hands those exact PNG bytes to the pipeline.
  • The same bytes come back to your browser as the displayed image.
  • So every block_bbox is already in image pixels - no conversion, no guessing.
  • One SVG with viewBox="0 0 width height" sits on top of the img and scales with it, so boxes stay put at any size.
  • Rotation and unwarping are switched off, so nothing invisible sits between a box and its pixels.

03Trust boundaries

OCR output is handled like any untrusted input:

  • Uploads are validated by decoding them and capped while streaming; CORS allows only localhost.
  • Block text is rendered as text, never as HTML.
  • Table HTML passes an nh3 allowlist server-side before anything is rendered.
  • Selection is keyed on stable block_ids, never on text - documents repeat text.
  • A failed run clears the previous result - you never see stale output.

04Storage and review - optional

Persistence is opt-in. A run stores nothing by itself - you inspect the result first, then decide to save it.

  • Save to history - one transaction writes the document, its pages and blocks; PNGs land in data/documents/<id>/, the DB keeps only their paths.
  • History page (/history) - everything you saved, searchable, with review counts and delete. /?doc=<id> reopens a document in the viewer.
  • Corrections - a fix is stored beside the original OCR text, never over it; later reads show the fix, the original stays.

05Stack and measured numbers

All numbers measured on the demo machine (Apple M2, 16 GB) - no claims beyond them.

ViewerNext.js 16.4.3 - React 19.3Upload, run, inspect, correct, save, download - one screen
APIFastAPI 0.162 - Python 3.11 (uv)Validates, normalizes, orchestrates; one envelope for every response
